prompt: Implement ChannelSwapper.swapRedBlue (red and blue trade places, green stays put) and ChannelSwapper.channelHistogramRed, which returns a 256-bucket count of the red values in an image.
explanation: Swapping channels needs no arithmetic at all -- unpack the three channels, then repack them in a different order as (b << 16) | (g << 8) | r. The histogram uses the channel value itself as an array index, which works precisely because a channel is always 0..255 and the array has exactly 256 slots. Incrementing counts[red] once per pixel is the classic counting-sort style tally: one pass over the image, no searching.
hints: For the swap, pull r, g and b out of the pixel as usual, then think about which channel each one belongs in when you shift them back.
A red channel is guaranteed to be between 0 and 255, so it can be used directly as an index into an int array of length 256.
Create int[] counts = new int[256] before the loops and do counts[red]++ for each pixel; Java already fills a new int array with zeros.
